page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the middle 50% tier. However, single-core performance is limited, as evidenced by a poor rating in stress-ng single-core tests. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show average throughput, although the PassMark memory score is classified as weak. The shared CPU allocation model introduces potential resource contention, which aligns with its positioning as a resource-dense but cost-efficient option for workloads requiring large memory footprints without intensive, sustained single-core CPU demands.

This server is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU performance or local NVMe storage. Appropriate use cases include caching layers, such as Redis deployments which achieve average transaction rates, in-memory databases, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks like software compilation and text processing.
